data.name: Leucine/BCAA restriction
data.description: Restriction of branched-chain amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, valine). Leucine reaches mTORC1 through Sestrin2 in the leading model, with LARS as a contested alternative. The effects are amino-acid- and sex-specific: in 3xTg mice, restricting isoleucine or valine improved metabolic health while restricting leucine did not (BAB2025).
data.description_beginner: Cutting back on branched-chain amino acids - leucine, isoleucine and valine - from the diet. Leucine is one of the main nutrients that switches mTORC1 on (Sestrin2 is the leading candidate sensor), so restricting these amino acids is one way researchers try to dial the pathway down. In one mouse study, cutting isoleucine or valine helped metabolic health but cutting leucine did not, and the effects differed between males and females.

studies.title: Restriction of individual branched-chain amino acids has distinct effects on the development and progression of Alzheimer's disease in 3xTg mice
studies.authors: Babygirija R; Lamming DW et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: UPDATE (was bioRxiv preprint at seed time, peer-reviewed and published in Advanced Science March 2026). Restricting individual branched-chain amino acids has distinct, sex-specific effects on cognition and AD pathology in 3xTg mice; restriction of isoleucine and valine (but not leucine) promotes metabolic health. Note: the different BCAAs act differentially on mTORC1, which is why single-amino-acid restriction matters.
